paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the Senior Marketing Manager position at Marcus & Millichap. I feel I have a lot of immediate value I can bring to your organization.

Your Corporate Marketing group needs someone who plans the work, sets scope and goals with internal stakeholders, and carries cross-functional projects to the finish. That is how I run my own company. At Lightbox Digital I delivered 98% of projects on time and 92% within budget while commanding teams of 5 to 20 people per project. At Grand Canyon Education I crystallized scope of work and synchronized with multiple departments with competing interests to meet and exceed stakeholder goals. I have used Wrike, Notion, Trello, and Workamajig for project management, so moving into Asana is a short step.

On the campaign side, at Charter One I created and led a video initiative that raised click-through rates for running ads by over 200%, and a social media content initiative that drove 20x more engagement than standard content. I have worked with residential real estate clients: I filmed model homes for Blandford Homes and photographed homes for realtors. I have produced creative work for seven years and can partner with your design team. My storyboards slashed back-and-forth communication by over 50%, and I hold a Master's in Marketing with a specialization in Marketing Analytics.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.

# NOT THE FULL POSTING: search-engine excerpts only

The full job description could not be retrieved. The text below is copied exactly from earlier WebSearch results (2026-10-14). It is the search engine's summary of Indeed listings, NOT Marcus & Millichap's wording. The posting's own headings, full responsibilities, requirements, qualifications and benefits text are missing. Get the real posting through the apply link before tailoring materials.

## WebSearch excerpt 1 (query: Marcus & Millichap "Senior Marketing Manager" remote 2026 agent experience job description)

It turned up several Indeed listings for a remote Senior Marketing Manager role at Marcus & Millichap, but none had a posting date, so I can't confirm they're from 2026. The results also don't show a requirement for agent experience specifically.

**What the listings describe:**
- The role focuses on strategy, planning, and project management for the firm's Corporate Marketing group, and includes developing campaigns and working with a design team. The position involves developing marketing campaigns, working with internal stakeholders to define project scope and goals, managing cross-functional projects, and partnering with the design team.
- Requirements: one listing asks for 10+ years of marketing or communications experience, strong project management and people leadership skills. Another asks for 8+ years in brand, integrated, or communications marketing, but that appears to be a different employer's listing that shares the page.
- Preferred extras: Commercial real estate experience and familiarity with Asana are strong pluses.
- Pay: The base salary range for this role is $85,000 – $100,000 per year.

## WebSearch excerpt 2 (query: "Marcus & Millichap" "Senior Marketing Manager" "Corporate Marketing" "$85,000" remote Asana commercial real estate)

This excerpt describes a December 2025 Marcus & Millichap listing titled "Marketing Manager". It is not confirmed to be this posting.

- **Marketing Manager, remote, Corporate Marketing:** A Marcus & Millichap listing dated December 2025 describes a role focused on strategy and project management for the firm's corporate marketing, and it is fully remote. The listing says the role sits in a cross-functional team and focuses on strategy, planning and project management for Corporate Marketing. It is a fully remote position. That listing gives no pay information. A separate Remotive posting for a remote Marketing Manager lists salary as unspecified, with a USA-only location.
- **Asana:** The December 2025 Phoenix-based Marketing Manager listing says experience with Asana is a strong plus. It also asks for 7+ years of experience in a Marketing or Communications role. That is a seniority level above the Marketing Manager title but may fit a senior-level search.

research.overview: Marcus & Millichap (NYSE: MMI) is a commercial real estate investment brokerage and financing firm. Its headquarters are in Calabasas, CA. It has 80+ offices and about 1,700 sales and financing professionals, who are mostly 100% commission agents and independent contractors. A smaller salaried corporate staff supports them. Andrew Strockis has been SVP / Chief Marketing Officer since November 2021. He came from Charles Schwab and oversees all corporate marketing and branding staff, and the company leadership page still lists him. Corporate marketing has posted fully remote roles recently: a Marketing Manager in Corporate Marketing (posted around December 2025, 5-10 years of experience, no pay listed) and a Senior Manager, Marketing Platforms & Production Solutions (around June 2026, $100k-$110k base). Finances: net loss of $12.4M in 2024, $1.9M in 2025 and $3.1M in Q1 2026. Q1 2026 revenue was $171.5M, and adjusted EBITDA turned positive. Most public employee reviews come from commission agents and brokers, not salaried corporate marketing staff. Marketing-specific evidence is limited to a Glassdoor Marketing Coordinator page (52 reviews, many likely from coordinators on broker teams), one 2016 Glassdoor Marketing Manager review, and one Indeed Marketing Manager review. The Indeed MCP tool failed to connect, so Indeed data comes from search results only.

glassdoor.review_count: About 1,100. Snapshots seen in search results show 1,079, 1,099 and 1,102.
glassdoor.summary: This is a company-wide score, and agents and brokers on commission dominate the reviews. 66-70% would recommend the company (the figure varies by snapshot), and 59% have a positive business outlook. Category scores: work-life balance 3.2, culture and values 3.5, career opportunities 3.7, compensation and benefits 2.9. The most common pro is training and hard-working colleagues (121 mentions). Common cons are 'management is terrible' (32 mentions) and 'no benefits package' (31), the second mostly from commission agents. Broker and agent sub-pages score far lower on work-life balance (1.7 and 2.4). For marketing staff, the Marketing Coordinator page shows 3.3 from 52 reviews, with only 23% recommending and compensation and benefits at 2.1. Reviewers there cite low pay, hourly pay and no advancement, and they praise training and culture. Many of these coordinators may sit on individual broker teams, not in corporate marketing. The only Marketing Manager review found is from 2016: it gave 3.0 and cited a lack of organization at the management level. That sample is old and very small. Search summaries say some snapshots are a year or more old.

indeed.summary: These are company-wide reviews, mostly from sales agents. The work wellbeing score is 69, from 115 survey responses. Stress-free scored below average and happiness above average. Reviewers describe two tracks: commission-only agents, and salaried staff employed by corporate or by individual top agents. One reviewer said agents get frequent training but analysts get less structured support. Reviewers also say each office is run by a regional manager and that pace and environment differ by office. One Marketing Manager in Los Angeles said the culture was good but the work became repetitive after a year, with not much room for growth. That is a single review. The Indeed MCP connector failed to connect, so these figures come from search result snippets, not the official data tool.

reddit.summary: Four searches (site:reddit.com, r/CommercialRealEstate, and 'reddit' combined with working, marketing and corporate terms) returned no Reddit threads about working at Marcus & Millichap. No Reddit evidence is used in this report.

pros.point: Corporate marketing hires remote roles. A Marketing Manager role in Corporate Marketing (around December 2025) was fully remote. A Senior Manager, Marketing Platforms & Production Solutions role (around June 2026) was also remote, with a posted base of $100k-$110k. That range is a useful comparison for the $85k-$100k band.

Marketing leadership has been stable. CMO Andrew Strockis joined in November 2021 from Charles Schwab, oversees all corporate marketing and branding, and is still listed on the leadership page. Searches found no reports of a CMO departure.
Training and coworkers are the most-praised items. 'Training was great' appears in 121 Glassdoor reviews, and Indeed reviewers mention frequent training. These are mostly agent reviews.

Some marketing staff describe a good culture. An Indeed Marketing Manager in LA called the culture good. Glassdoor Marketing Coordinator reviewers praised culture and the team's use of Asana. A small CareerBliss sample from the Calabasas HQ (2 reviews) described a relaxed setting with a casual dress code.
Salaried staff get standard benefits. Built In lists performance bonuses, health and dental insurance, and a 401(k). The 'no benefits' complaints on Glassdoor come mostly from commission agents.

Results are improving. The net loss fell from $12.4M (2024) to $1.9M (2025). In Q1 2026 revenue rose to $171.5M and adjusted EBITDA turned positive. The firm also won a GlobeSt Best Place to Work award two years in a row (per a 2024 release).

cons.point: Pay gets the lowest scores. Glassdoor compensation and benefits is 2.9 company-wide and 2.1 on the Marketing Coordinator page. RepVue rates base pay 1.8 out of 47 ratings, mostly from sales roles. Payscale estimates for a Marketing Manager in New York run $39k-$69k. These are estimates, not verified pay.

Marketing staff report limited growth. The Glassdoor Marketing Coordinator page scores 3.3 from 52 reviews, with 23% recommending and complaints of no advancement. An Indeed Marketing Manager said the work became repetitive after a year. CareerBliss rates growth opportunities 3.2.

Corporate staff, not brokers, have taken past cuts. In 2020 the firm cut about 20% of its salaried workforce. In December 2023 it reduced headcount again, and a spokesperson said the cuts were limited to corporate staff while the firm kept hiring agents.

Work-life balance and stress scores are below average. Glassdoor work-life balance is 3.2. Indeed rates stress-free below average. 'The management is terrible' appears in 32 Glassdoor reviews. The one Marketing Manager review (2016) cited a lack of organization at the management level.

The company is still losing money in a slow deal market. It posted a net loss in 2024, 2025 and Q1 2026. In the Q2 2026 call, the CEO said deal timelines remain long and that headcount growth will come more slowly, through internships and fellowships.

The culture centers on brokers and varies by office. Indeed reviewers say each office is run by its own regional manager. Job postings describe a commission-driven, 'work hard, play hard' setting. Corporate marketing serves about 1,700 agents, which can mean many internal stakeholders with sales-first priorities.

red_flags: Past layoffs fell on salaried corporate staff: about 20% of salaried staff in 2020, and corporate-only cuts in December 2023. A corporate marketing role sits in that group.
Net losses continued through Q1 2026, although they are narrowing.
The Glassdoor Marketing Coordinator page shows only 23% would recommend (52 reviews, mixed and partly old, and many likely from coordinators on broker teams).
No company-wide remote or return-to-office policy was found, and some corporate roles are posted as in-office. Get the remote arrangement for this role in writing.
SEC filings flag a pending case (TwinRock Holdings v. Southside Ventures) with possible effects on the brokerage business. Searches did not confirm details or status.
Marketing-specific evidence is thin: one 2016 Marketing Manager review, one Indeed Marketing Manager review, and no Reddit discussion.
research.bottom_line: Company-wide ratings are average: Glassdoor 3.7 (about 1,100 reviews) and Indeed 3.4 (about 267 reviews). Both are driven mostly by commission agents, so they say little about salaried corporate marketing. The marketing-specific signals are weaker. They point to low pay scores, limited growth, and a history of corporate staff being the ones cut when deals slow down. On the plus side, the corporate marketing team hires remote, the CMO has been in place since 2021, and losses are shrinking. The $85k-$100k band sits below the $100k-$110k posted for a Senior Manager role on the same team in June 2026, so Joshua should aim for the top of the band or higher. In interviews, he should ask about team size and reporting line (does the role report to the CMO?), whether remote is permanent, how marketing fared in the December 2023 cuts, and how the team handles requests from about 1,700 brokers. It is worth pursuing with clear eyes, but not a standout employer on the available evidence.
